glance.job: document to infographic, every number exact
glance.prompt:
Here is a document. Create one infographic that tells its whole story clearly, with every number exactly as written and no numbers other than those given.

DOCUMENT
Title: php2shell, where it stands on 22 October 2026
Two critical security flaws were found in PHP itself, the engine that runs WordPress and millions of other websites. Both are rated 9.2 out of 10. Anyone on the internet, with no password, can make an unpatched web server run their own commands.
The fix came out on 21 October 2026 in four versions: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Versions 8.1 and older have no ready-made fix.
Attackers are trying: one internet security company counted millions of attempts. But zero organisations have confirmed a break-in, and the US government's list of flaws known to be used in attacks does not include these two.
16 government cyber agencies all say: install the fix now. If you cannot, they disagree: take it offline, isolate it, or restrict it.
Phones and laptops are not the target; web servers are.
Bottom line: update PHP, restart it, and decide now who can take a system offline.

LAYOUT: a square infographic. The title at the top. Then four big stat tiles in a row: 9.2 (severity out of 10), 4 (fixed versions), millions (attack attempts), 0 (confirmed break-ins). Below them, a simple left-to-right picture: an attacker figure sending a request through the internet to a web server, with a green shield labelled 'the fix' blocking it. At the bottom, a banner with the bottom line. Style: a bold, modern editorial infographic. Deep midnight navy background, white and pale lavender type, one hot coral-red accent for danger and one emerald green accent for the fix. Flat vector shapes, generous spacing, large clean sans-serif lettering, crisp edges, no gradients behind text, no photographs, no logos, no brand marks, no watermark. Spell every word correctly. No other text.

how.prompt:

Step 2: 'Sends one web request. No password.' (icon: an envelope flying along a line).

To the right of steps 3 to 5, a tall emerald-green vertical shield labelled 'Patched and restarted: the request fails'.
Title at the very top: 'How the attack works'. Style: a bold, modern editorial infographic. Deep midnight navy background, white and pale lavender type, one hot coral-red accent for danger and one emerald green accent for the fix. Flat vector shapes, generous spacing, large clean sans-serif lettering, crisp edges, no gradients behind text, no photographs, no logos, no brand marks, no watermark. Use exactly the words given, spelled exactly. No numbers other than the step numbers 1 to 5. No other text.
